governing_table.code: No statewide building or plumbing code for private buildings: each city or county adopts its own. Model code used here: International Building Code and International Plumbing Code in the edition the Kansas Department of Administration applies to construction on State property (Form 110). For school buildings, K.S.A. 31-150 and K.A.R. 22-18-3 require the International Building Code adopted in K.A.R. 22-1-3 (2006 edition), which was not read.
governing_table.edition: 2018 (model text as used on State property; each city's edition and amendments differ)
governing_table.table: IBC Table 2902.1 (same table as IPC Table 403.1), with IBC Sections 2902.1.1 and 2902.2 and IPC Section 424.2
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space. Uses not shown in Table 2902.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code.
governing_table.statewide_code_quote: The State of Kansas enforces building codes for projects on State of Kansas owned property. It does not enforce a statewide building code, but authorizes local jurisdictions to adopt local building codes.

Chapter 11, Accessibility, is deleted. See Item N below. ... F. International Plumbing Code (IPC), 2018 Edition. ... N. K.S.A. 58-1301, et seq. – 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (2010 ADA Standards).
governing_table.schools_quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the construction, reconstruction or renovation of school buildings shall comply with the requirements of the 2000 edition of the international building code as published by the international codes council. ... (g) The state fire marshal shall adopt rules and regulations specifying those subsequent editions of the codes enumerated in subsections (a) and (b) which the state fire marshal has determined provide protection equivalent to those editions specified herein.

sex_split.text: The total occupant load is divided in half, one half for each sex, unless approved statistical data show a different split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, for each sex.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational occupancies and up to 50% in all other occupancies, offices included. Each urinal needs a privacy partition.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
urinal_substitution.quote_partitions: 1209.3.1 Water Closet Compartment Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. ... 1209.3.2 Urinal Partitions Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate rooms for each sex are not required where the total occupant load, employees and customers together, is 15 or fewer, in a business occupancy of 25 or fewer, or in a mercantile occupancy of 100 or fewer.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 2902.2 Separate Facilities Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 square feet gross per occupant. Restaurant dining room (assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 square feet net. Classroom: 20 square feet net.
occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net ... Business areas 150 gross ... Educational Classroom area 20 net

hdpe_fire.section: No statewide building code, so no state rule. Model text: 2018 International Building Code Section 803.9, pointing to Section 803.1.1 (NFPA 286), the edition Kansas applies on State property (Form 110).
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP) Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. ... 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1.
hdpe_fire.note: The section speaks of HDPE or polypropylene 'used as an interior finish' and does not name toilet partitions. It applies on State property (2018 IBC, Form 110) and in any city that adopted the 2012 or a later IBC without deleting it. The 2006 IBC named in K.A.R. 22-1-3 (State Fire Marshal, school buildings) was not read; whether that edition has an HDPE rule is open.

access.state_standard: K.S.A. 58-1301 et seq. makes the federal ADA Title II (28 C.F.R. Part 35) and Title III (28 C.F.R. Part 36) regulations state law; Kansas has no separate technical standard. The Department of Administration states that the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design are 'the effective federal and state accessibility requirements'. A city's building code may add ICC A117.1 through IBC Chapter 11 (2009 edition under the 2018 IBC); on State property Chapter 11 is deleted and only the 2010 ADA Standards apply.
access.state_standard_quote: 58-1301. ... all existing facilities, and the design and construction of all new, additions to and alterations of, facilities in this state shall conform to Title II or Title III, as appropriate.
access.state_standard_quote_2: All buildings on State-Owned Property are subject to federal [28 CFR Part 35] and state accessibility laws, (K.S.A. 58-1301 et seq.), which mirror Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (2010 ADA Standards) are the effective federal and state accessibility requirements.

differences.point: State law itself: no difference for stalls. Kansas adopts the federal regulations by reference and sets no stall dimensions of its own.
differences.state: K.S.A. 58-1301b(c) and (d): "'Title II' means 28 C.F.R. Part 35 ... 'Title III' means 28 C.F.R. Part 36, nondiscrimination on the basis of disability by public accommodations and commercial facilities"
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards sections 213 and 604 apply unchanged.
differences.quote: (d) "Title III" means 28 C.F.R. Part 36, nondiscrimination on the basis of disability by public accommodations and commercial facilities as required by section 301 et seq. of the Americans with disabilities act of 1990, 42 U.S.C.A. § 12,181 et seq., as amended by the ADA amendments act of 2008.

differences.point: Not a stall rule: Kansas requires the wheelchair symbol at the entrance of facilities that comply.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 216.6 requires the symbol only at accessible entrances where not all entrances are accessible (federal text not re-read for this point).
differences.quote: The international symbol of access to individuals with a disability shall be permanently displayed at the entrance of all facilities that are in compliance with the standards established pursuant to this act.

differences.point: Only where a city's building code keeps IBC Chapter 11 (not state law): ICC A117.1-2009 adds an 18 inch vertical grab bar on the side wall of the wheelchair stall.
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 Section 604.5.1 (read on UpCodes), referenced by 2018 IBC Section 1102.1: "Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with this code and ICC A117.1."
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: "The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall." No vertical bar.
differences.quote: In addition, a vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.point: Only where a city's building code keeps IBC Chapter 11: the count of ambulatory stalls reads slightly differently but gives the same result in practice.
differences.state: 2018 IBC 1109.2.2: "Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment."
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: "at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures."
differences.quote: Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible.

access.process: No state plan review or registration for private buildings. K.S.A. 58-1304 assigns enforcement: for private and other facilities, 'the building inspector or other agency or person designated by the governmental entity in which the facility is located'; local government buildings, the local government itself; State property, the Secretary of Administration (the Office of Facilities and Property Management and the State ADA Coordinator review every project); public school (K-12) buildings, the State Board of Education by plan approval under K.S.A. 31-150, with plans sealed by a Kansas-licensed architect or engineer. The Attorney General oversees enforcement and may seek an injunction (K.S.A. 58-1308).
access.process_quote: (4) for the design and construction of all other new, additions to and alterations of, facilities which are subject to the provisions of this act, the building inspector or other agency or person designated by the governmental entity in which the facility is located. (b) The attorney general of the state of Kansas shall oversee the enforcement of this act.
access.confidence_note: State statutes read on ksrevisor.gov. A117.1-2009 and IBC Chapter 11 read on UpCodes (secondary); whether they apply depends on the city's code.

single_user.rule: No Kansas statute or statewide code sets rules for single-user restrooms in private buildings. The 2026 law on government buildings expressly allows single-occupancy rooms there, including a unisex single-toilet restroom with a locking door and family restrooms. The model 2018 building code that cities build on says single-user rooms 'shall be identified for use by either sex'; the city's adopted code governs.
single_user.quote: "Single-occupancy private space" means a facility designed or designated for use by only one individual at a time and in which the individual may be in a state of undress. "Single-occupancy private space" includes, but is not limited to: (A) A single toilet restroom with a locking door that is designed or designated as unisex; or (B) a family restroom or changing room. ... (2) This subsection shall not be construed to prohibit a governing body ... from: ... (B) establishing a single-occupancy private space.
single_user.model_quote: Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified for use by either sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: Private buildings: no state law; the city's building code decides. The model 2018 code requires separate facilities for each sex (Section 2902.2) and has no provision for a shared all-gender multi-stall room. Government buildings: not allowed. Each restroom designed for more than one person in a building owned or leased by a governmental entity must be designated for one sex, 'regardless of whether the facility provides curtains or partial walls for privacy'.
all_gender_shared.quote: The governing body, or chief administrative officer if no governing body exists, of each public building shall designate each multiple-occupancy private space in such building for use only by individuals of one sex.
all_gender_shared.model_quote: 2902.2 Separate Facilities Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex.

use_restrictions.rule: 2026 Session Laws of Kansas, Chapter 3 (House Substitute for Senate Bill 244), in force since publication in the Kansas Register on February 26, 2026. Applies to 'public buildings': buildings owned or leased by a governmental entity (as defined in K.S.A. 75-6102, not read), except a government-owned building leased to a private entity under a lease in force on the effective date. Multiple-occupancy restrooms, locker rooms, changing rooms and shower rooms must be designated for one sex. Exceptions for custodial, maintenance, emergency, assistance, law enforcement and coaching purposes, and for a child under nine with a carer. A governmental entity that violates the section is liable for $25,000 for the first violation and $125,000 for each later one. It does not apply to privately owned buildings.
use_restrictions.quote: "Public building" means a building owned or leased by a governmental entity. "Public building" does not include a building owned by a governmental entity that is leased to a private entity, whether for profit or not for profit, if the lease agreement for such building between the governmental entity and the private entity was in force and effect on the effective date of this act. ... (d) Any governmental entity that violates this section is liable for a civil penalty of $25,000 for the first violation and $125,000 for each subsequent violation. ... Sec. 9. This act shall take effect and be in force from and after its publication in the Kansas register. ... Published in the Kansas Register February 26, 2026.

public_wage.law: None. Kansas's former public works wage statute, K.S.A. 44-201, was repealed in 1987. K.S.A. 12-16,130 and 12-16,131 (2013) bar cities, counties and local government units from requiring construction contractors to pay more than the minimum wage unless state or federal law requires it. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded work.
public_wage.rates_url: https://sam.gov/wage-determinations (federal Davis-Bacon wage determinations; applies to federally funded work only)
public_wage.quote: 44-201. History: R.S. 1923, 44-201; L. 1931, ch. 214, § 1; L. 1947, ch. 286, § 1; Repealed, L. 1987, ch. 186, § 1; July 1. || 12-16,131. (a) No city, county or local government unit shall enact or administer any ordinance, resolution or law that requires, nor shall any city, county or local government discriminate against, favor, prefer or base any ordinance, law, policy, economic development program, agreement, grant or incentive on, an employer providing or not providing: ... (3) compensation or wages at any rate higher than the minimum wage, unless the payment of higher compensation or wages is required by state or federal law ... (b) Subsection (a) shall only apply to wages, compensation or benefits, or any combination thereof, paid or provided by a construction contractor or subcontractor performing construction or infrastructure work on a real estate construction or infrastructure project.
public_wage.confidence_note: Statutes read on ksrevisor.gov. No Kansas Department of Labor page stating 'no prevailing wage law' was opened; the Davis-Bacon statement follows from the absence of a state law and was not read on a federal page.

sales_tax.state_rate_quote: The Kansas statewide sales (and use) tax rate is 6.5%. In addition to the state sales tax, Kansas counties, incorporated cities and special taxing districts may impose a local sales tax. Local sales tax rates currently range from .10% to 3%.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. Goods shipped to a Kansas customer are taxed at the state and local rate in effect at the delivery address. An out-of-state (remote) seller must collect Kansas retailers' compensating use tax once its sales into Kansas exceed $100,000 in a calendar year. Where the seller does not collect, the buyer owes consumers' compensating use tax directly to the Department of Revenue, at the same rate.
shipped_goods.quote: Use tax is due on out-of-state purchases whether the property is shipped into Kansas or picked up in another state and brought back to Kansas. ... There are two types of compensating use tax: (1) Retailers' Compensating Use Tax, which is collected by retailers in other states from their Kansas customers; and (2) Consumers' Compensating Use Tax, which is paid by the Kansas consumer directly to the Department of Revenue. ... A "remote seller" is required to begin collecting and remitting tax on sales in excess of the $100,000 threshold as soon as they cross the threshold.

freight.rule: Since July 1, 2023, delivery charges (shipping, postage, handling, crating and packing) are not taxed when they are stated separately on the invoice and reflect a true or reasonable cost of delivery. Freight included in the price and not stated separately is taxed.
freight.quote: Beginning July 1, 2023, charges to the customer for handling and delivery are not subject to tax when separately stated on the invoice. To qualify for the exclusion from the sales tax base, delivery charges that are separately stated on the invoice, bill of sale, or similar document provided to the purchaser must be clearly denominated as charges for: (1) delivery; (2) transmission; or (3) transportation AND must be representative of a true or reasonable cost of delivery. Delivery charges may include shipping, postage, handling, crating and packing. ... NOTE: Freight and postage are taxable ONLY when they are not separately stated on the invoice and included as part of a total sale between the retailer and the customer.

install_labor.rule: Taxable on a commercial remodel, whether or not billed separately, at the rate in effect at the job site. Labor on the original construction of a building or facility, and labor at a residence, is exempt.
install_labor.quote: GENERAL RULES: RESIDENTIAL LABOR–EXEMPT; ORIGINAL CONSTRUCTION–EXEMPT; COMMERCIAL REMODEL–TAXABLE. ... Taxable labor services in Kansas are the services of installing, applying, servicing, repairing, altering, or maintaining tangible personal property performed on real property projects in the general category of commercial remodel work. The rate of sales tax due on the labor portion on the invoice is the rate of sales tax in effect where the installation/application took place. ... Examples of taxable labor services performed in, on or around an existing commercial building or facility include but are not limited to: remodeling its interior or exterior

furnish_and_install.rule: The contractor is the final consumer of the materials it installs and pays sales or use tax when buying them; it cannot buy them for resale. On a commercial remodel it then collects sales tax from the customer on the labor part of the contract: total receipts less tax-paid materials and tax-paid subcontractors, with profit and overhead included in the taxed amount. On original construction the labor is exempt, so the customer is charged no tax on the contract.
furnish_and_install.quote: All contractors (whether contractors or contractor-retailers) are considered to be the final user or consumer of the materials they install for others, and must pay Kansas sales or use tax on them. ... The sales tax base for construction contracts is the total amount of money received for completion of a job or project, known as your gross receipts, less: cost of direct materials (on which sales or use tax has been paid or accrued), and payments to subcontractors (on which sales tax has been paid, when applicable).

sales_tax.confidence_note: Read in Publications KS-1525 and KS-1510, both revised 7-29-25, on ksrevenue.gov. Statutes (K.S.A. 79-3603, 79-3702) not opened.

page.stalls_intro: Kansas has no statewide building code, so each city sets its own toilet counts. The model rules Kansas cities build on, which the state uses for its own buildings, count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area, with half counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen.
page.stalls_after: These figures come from the model rules, before any city changes. They are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: The model rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Kansas has no statewide building code, so this rule comes from your city's code. The model rules Kansas cities build on, which the state uses for its own buildings, require solid plastic (HDPE) used as an interior finish to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes, and Kansas law makes the federal rules state law without adding its own. Kansas has no state review of plans for access in private buildings: the city's building inspector checks it.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Kansas and federal stall rules match:** Kansas law adopts the federal access rules as they stand, so it sets no stall sizes of its own. Where a city's building code applies the national accessibility standard, that standard also asks for an 18 inch vertical grab bar on the side wall next to the toilet.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** in private buildings, Kansas has no state law on single-user or all-gender restrooms, so the city's building code decides how a one-person restroom is signed and whether a shared all-gender room is allowed. In buildings owned or leased by a government body, a Kansas law in force since February 2026 requires every restroom built for more than one person to be designated for one sex. One-person and family restrooms are still allowed there.
page.public_jobs: Kansas has no state wage law for public construction, and state law bars cities and counties from setting wage rates for construction contractors, so set wage rates apply only on federally funded jobs.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Kansas, labor to install partitions in an existing commercial building is taxed, even when it's billed separately. Labor on the original construction of a building is not. A contractor who supplies and installs partitions pays the tax when buying them and charges tax on the labor part of the job.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable at the rate for the delivery address. Delivery charges listed separately on the invoice are not taxed. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Kansas Department of Revenue
